matchups.analysis: Rob's sitting at 53% with ESPN projecting 107.0 to Flamur's 101.2—that's a five-point edge that holds up if his depth crew (Kyren Williams, Kenyon Sadiq, Marcus Mariota) actually executes instead of becoming the kind of mid-tier waiver wire disappointments that blow up close matchups. Flamur's got the sexier top-two in CeeDee and Saquon, but Rob's receiving trio with McCaffrey, Rashee Rice, and Garrett Wilson is legitimately more floor-friendly across the board, which is why ESPN's giving him the slight nod when both of you are basically playing from zero. Neither team torched their own lineup this week, so this comes down to pure roster execution and whether Rob's nine starters hit their marks consistently or whether Flamur's steadier secondary layer (Tee Higgins, Chase Brown, Trevor Lawrence) decides to make up the projection gap. Still plenty of football left to play, but Rob should feel slightly less sketchy than Flamur about whether his bench depth actually shows up when it matters.
